note: Hand-edited. aliases = names riders use. misspellings = starter guesses, not collected from real use. Order and river miles: Wikipedia list of Willamette crossings. Ends, carries, colors marked colors_verified=true: Wikipedia bridge pages. Colors with colors_verified=false come from photo captions. Positions are generated into bridges.json by tools/build_bridges.py.

st-johns.name: St. Johns Bridge

ends.east: St. Johns and Cathedral Park, North Portland

st-johns.bike_facility: Sidewalks on both sides, bicycles allowed (OpenStreetMap)

fremont.name: Fremont Bridge
fremont.bike_note: Freeway. Bicycles and pedestrians prohibited (OpenStreetMap: motorway, bicycle=no).
fremont.bike_facility: None. I-405 is closed to bikes and pedestrians in its entirety (OAR 734-020-0045)

broadway.name: Broadway Bridge

ends.west: Pearl District and Old Town via NW Broadway and the Lovejoy ramp

broadway.bike_facility: Two 11 ft sidewalks plus bike paths (Wikipedia, OpenStreetMap)
broadway.transit: Portland Streetcar A and B Loops (Wikipedia)

steel.name: Steel Bridge
steel.carries: Upper deck: road and MAX. Lower deck: Union Pacific rail and the bike and pedestrian walkway
steel.bike_note: Use the lower deck walkway (south side, built 2001 with the Eastbank Esplanade). Upper deck has narrow sidewalks.
steel.bike_facility: Lower deck walkway, separated from traffic (Wikipedia). Narrow sidewalks on the upper deck

burnside.name: Burnside Bridge

ends.west: Old Town, Saturday Market under the west end
ends.east: Central Eastside, Burnside Skatepark under the east end; stairs to the Eastbank Esplanade

burnside.bike_note: Bike lanes since 1995. Earthquake Ready Burnside Bridge replacement: construction set to begin 2026, opening by 2031 (Wikipedia). Expect closures.

morrison.name: Morrison Bridge
morrison.bike_facility: Barrier-separated path on the south side, 2009 (Wikipedia)

hawthorne.name: Hawthorne Bridge

ends.west: Downtown at SW Naito Pkwy and 1st Ave
ends.east: Central Eastside at SE Grand Ave and MLK Blvd

hawthorne.bike_note: Busiest bicycle and transit bridge in the state (Multnomah County). Eastbound bikes use the south side, westbound the north side.
hawthorne.bike_facility: 10 ft sidewalks on both sides used by bikes; eastbound south, westbound north (Wikipedia, Multnomah County)

marquam.name: Marquam Bridge

ends.east: Inner Southeast industrial area near the I-84 interchange (freeway)

marquam.bike_facility: None. I-5 north of the Beaverton-Tigard interchange is closed to bikes and pedestrians (OAR 734-020-0045)

tilikum.name: Tilikum Crossing
tilikum.carries: MAX Orange Line, buses, streetcar, bike and pedestrian path; no cars
tilikum.bike_note: No private cars. 14 ft bike and pedestrian paths on both sides. 'Bridge of the People' is the official full name (Wikipedia); 'Caruthers Crossing' and 'Portland-Milwaukie Light Rail Bridge' were pre-naming names.

ends.west: South Waterfront, OHSU/South Waterfront MAX station
ends.east: Central Eastside near OMSI, OMSI MAX station

tilikum.bike_facility: 14 ft paths on both sides (Wikipedia). No private cars
tilikum.transit: MAX Orange Line; TriMet 9 (TriMet schedule) and 19 (since August 2023, TriMet release); Portland Streetcar (Wikipedia)

ross-island.name: Ross Island Bridge
ross-island.bike_note: No bike facilities listed (Wikipedia). One walkway on the north side with no barrier from the westbound lane. Engine avoids it. Not offered until a rider confirms it (B-07).

ends.west: Naito Pkwy interchange, SW Kelly Ave and Porter St (walkway)

ross-island.bike_facility: One north-side walkway with no barrier from the westbound lane. No bike facilities listed (Wikipedia)
ross-island.transit: None found. TriMet Line 9 (Powell) crosses on Tilikum (TriMet schedule page), and Line 19 moved to Tilikum in August 2023 to avoid Ross Island Bridge congestion (TriMet release)

sellwood.name: Sellwood Bridge

ends.west: OR 43 / Macadam Ave, Willamette Greenway Trail
ends.east: Sellwood and Westmoreland at SE Tacoma St; Springwater Trail nearby

sellwood.bike_facility: Bike lanes in both directions and sidewalks on both sides (Wikipedia)

interstate-5.name: Interstate Bridge
interstate-5.carries: I-5; shared paths on both sides
interstate-5.bike_note: Bike and pedestrian paths on both sides (OpenStreetMap: path, bicycle=designated). Riders describe them as narrow; width not verified. Lift span opens about 250 times a year (Interstate Bridge Replacement program). Replacement bridge approved; existing bridge stays in use during construction.

ends.south: Hayden Island, Portland (reach it from Marine Drive and Delta Park over the North Portland Harbor path)
ends.north: Downtown Vancouver, WA, at the Columbia River waterfront

interstate-5.bike_facility: Paths on both sides, separate from the freeway lanes (OpenStreetMap). Width not verified
interstate-5.transit: C-TRAN, likely route 60 to Delta Park (inferred, not confirmed)

interstate-205.name: Glenn L. Jackson Memorial Bridge
interstate-205.carries: I-205; two-way bike and pedestrian path in the center
interstate-205.bike_note: 9 ft two-way path between the two freeway structures (Wikipedia), behind a low concrete wall and railings (BikePortland). No access to Government Island. Part of the I-205 Multi-Use Path.

ends.south: Near NE Airport Way and Marine Drive, Portland; Marine Drive Trail and 40 Mile Loop
ends.north: East Vancouver, WA, near SE Evergreen Hwy; Veterans Memorial Greenway

interstate-205.bike_facility: 9 ft two-way path in the center behind a low wall and railings (Wikipedia, BikePortland)
interstate-205.transit: C-TRAN, likely route 65 to Parkrose (inferred, not confirmed)

blumenauer.name: Congressman Earl Blumenauer Bicycle and Pedestrian Bridge
blumenauer.carries: Bikes and pedestrians only, 24 ft wide, 475 ft long
blumenauer.bike_note: Car-free link over I-84 and the Union Pacific Railroad at NE 7th Ave. Opened July 31, 2022. Northeast link of the Green Loop. Preferred (Whitney): prioritize it.
blumenauer.bike_facility: 24 ft car-free bike and pedestrian bridge (KPFF)

categories.mixed_use: Mixed use bridge: cars, bikes, and pedestrians share the bridge, on separate lanes, paths, or sidewalks. May also carry buses, streetcar, or rail.
categories.transit_and_pedestrian: Transit and pedestrian bridge: TriMet (MAX, bus, streetcar), bikes, and pedestrians. No private cars.
categories.pedestrian_only: Pedestrian only bridge: bikes and pedestrians only, no motor vehicles.
categories.car_only: Car only bridge: freeway, closed to bikes and pedestrians. Never offered.
categories.freeway_with_path: Freeway bridge with a separate bike and pedestrian path.
categories.pedestrian_overpass: Pedestrian overpass: a bike and pedestrian bridge over a road, freeway, or railway.
categories.mixed_use_overpass: Mixed use overpass: a road overpass with a bike lane.
categories.rail_only: Rail only bridge: trains only. Never offered.
